method: Question: when an EDGE EXH label (Tier 1, the first trigger) fires, does it reach its own target before its own stop, and does the state of the MAs and of CVD at that moment help? A T2 (MA cross) or T3 (PC cross) normally follows, in either order. Method: I read each label (entry, target, stop) from your 4H screenshots, then followed the price on the chart to see which was hit first. Targets are about 3 times the stop on every label I checked. MA state = green line above or below the orange line on the label's bar. CVD state = whether the CVD pane was falling or rising in the label's direction over the last few bars. Where I could not read a state, it says Not read. These are chart readings, not exact data.

findings.title: The raw results flatter the labels
findings.body: This window holds two big trends, many labels are the same move counted more than once, and I let each label run for up to about 4 weeks. Do not read the R total as something to expect.

findings.title: Buy labels during the fall lost
findings.body: On gold and silver, the buy labels that appeared while price was dropping (23 Oct, 13 Nov, and 4 Nov on silver) were all stopped out. The 20 Nov gold buy is still open and CVD is against it.

findings.title: Early sells at tops lost often
findings.body: Sell labels that fired late Oct to early Nov, while the MAs were still bullish, were stopped out on CADJPY (2 of 3), GBPJPY (2 of 2), USDJPY (2) and gold (1 of 3). On AUDJPY the same kind of sells all won, but slowly, taking up to 2.5 weeks. The MA state is read for only some of them, so treat this as a lead to check.

findings.title: EDGE EXH fires first, the cross follows
findings.body: EDGE EXH is Tier 1 and is the first logic to trigger. The MA cross (T2) or the PC cross (T3) follows, in either order. So at the moment of the label the MAs usually still point the other way, and only 4 of the labels I could read agreed with them. That is how the system is built, not a flaw. The MA state at the label is not the test. The test is what happens after: did a same-direction T2 or T3 follow, and how much of the move was left.

findings.title: CVD: agreeing went with targets, against went with stops
findings.body: See the CVD bars above for the counts. Only gold and silver have been read so far, so it is a hint, not evidence. The one winner with CVD against was the early top sell on gold (5 Nov).

findings.title: The best sells came before the cross
findings.body: On gold, the EDGE EXH sells at 4,127 (5 Nov) and 4,141 (9 Nov) fired while the MAs were still bullish and CVD was not falling. Both won. The red MA cross came about 2 days later, near 4,080. A rule that waits for the cross and for CVD to agree would have entered about 50 points lower. The cost of the earlier entry is more false tops: the 28 Oct sell was stopped out by about 0.3 points.

findings.title: CVD resets every week
findings.body: On 4H the CVD pane resets on Monday, so the line jumps. A buy can look like rising CVD only because of the jump (silver, 4 Nov, which was stopped out). Read the dashboard CVD TREND row (5 bars) or exported numbers, not the picture at a reset.

findings.title: Next steps
findings.body: 1) For each label, record whether a same-direction T2 (MA cross) or T3 (PC cross) followed, which came first, how many bars later, and how much of the move was left at that point. MA crosses can be read from the + markers. PC crosses need the alert log, Discord, or the Plus export. 2) Compare labels that got a follow-up with labels that did not. 3) Read the 5-bar CVD trend at every label (only gold and silver so far). 4) Cap the holding time (for example 5 days) so slow wins do not flatter the result.
